description: This tool from the SearchWing project plans search and rescue missions for fixed-wing drones automatically. The user enters the drone's range and camera angles, the smallest object that must be detectable, the take-off point, the estimated position of the person or object sought, the landing point, the wind and the time available, and the tool computes a search pattern and flight mission, including the highest altitude at which the object can still be detected. The calculations follow a 2019 SearchWing paper on search area calculations by Friedrich Beckmann, and wind is used to estimate fixed-wing flight efficiency. It has a Python back end, which can also be used from the command line, and an Angular web front end. The source is free to download from GitLab under the GPL-3.0-or-later licence. Caveats: it is a planning tool for one drone type and relies on an estimated search position, and the repository does not report field validation. Coverage is general. Simulation uses: estimating how much area drone patrols can cover in search and rescue, as part of emergency service capacity studies. Related records: the Basarnas SAR statistics (data-basarnas-indonesia-sar-statistics) give search and rescue operations data for Indonesia.
